text: @stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 是面向 DSH 网页端的可复用提示词库，在 Settings 中提供管理页面，并在聊天输入区加入提示词选择器。用户可以创建、编辑、删除和搜索指令，按会话勾选要注入的内容，也能设置新会话默认启用项；未单独选择的子 agent 会继承最近祖先会话的选择。选中的指令会作为运行时上下文供模型步骤使用。适合需要跨会话复用工作规范、语气或任务指令的 DSH 用户。保存内容需要可写的 profile settings 文件，不需要额外 API key。

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib adds reusable prompts to DSH web. Edit them in Settings, then search and select instructions per chat. New chats can use defaults; subagents inherit the nearest ancestor's selection. Chosen text enters model context. Saving needs writable profile settings; no API key.
我想把常用的工作指令存起来，在不同聊天里按需启用。
能不能给每个会话单独挑选要遵循的提示词？
让新开的聊天自动带上我设定好的默认指令。
我希望子 agent 沿用启动它的聊天所选的提示词。
想在设置里维护自己的指令模板，随时修改或删掉。
聊天时能快速搜索提示词并勾选多条组合使用吗？
I want reusable instructions that I can turn on separately for each chat.
Can new sessions start with my chosen prompts already enabled?
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 的功能「提示词管理」：在 Settings → Prompts 中创建、编辑、删除指令并设置新会话默认项。填写标题和正文后保存到插件配置。
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 的功能「会话选择器」：在聊天输入区打开 Prompts 面板，搜索并勾选要使用的提示词；选择按当前会话保存，也可清空。
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 的功能「会话上下文注入」：模型组装步骤时读取当前会话所选指令，将正文合并成运行时上下文；未选内容时不注入文本。
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 的功能「子 agent 继承」：会话没有自己的选择时，沿 parentSession 查找最近祖先的提示词选择；整条会话链都没有选择时采用默认项。
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib 使用前须知：DSH profile 的 settings 文件必须可写，提示词和会话选择才能保存；写入失败时页面会显示错误。（见 client.js:119-122）

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · @stmol/dsh-prompt-lib：🥷 Keep your own prompts inside [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), and switch them on for a chat in one click.

- **Settings → Prompts**: write, edit and delete your prompts.
- **Chat composer**: tick the ones you want for this session. The button shows how many are on.

A prompt that is ticked applies to every model step of that session, and to the subagents it starts.
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · @stmol/dsh-prompt-lib：

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Install：Published on npm as [`@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib).
Any bundle source works: the npm package, the [repository](https://github.com/Stmol/dsh-prompt-lib), a tarball, or a local folder.

- **GUI:** Settings → Plugins → Add plugin, then `@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib`.
- **CLI:** `dsh plugin add @stmol/dsh-prompt-lib`.

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Install：Restart DSH after the first install; later edits reach the running app through HMR. There are no automatic updates: remove the plugin and add it again.

<details>
<summary>Install from a local checkout</summary>

```bash
dsh plugin add link:/path/to/dsh-prompt-lib
```

A linked checkout keeps its own `node_modules`, so the plugin's one dependency has to be installed there too:

```bash
cd /path/to/dsh-prompt-lib && npm install
```

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Install：Without it the plugin fails to load and nothing appears in Settings.

</details>

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Usage：1. Open **Settings → Prompts**. It is its own page, after *Agent presets*. Write a title and an instruction, then save.
   - The title is a label for you. The list, the search field and the composer picker use it to keep prompts findable. It is never sent to the model, only the instruction text is.
   - The instruction is stored in the plugin's config, so it survives restarts and is there in every session.
   - **Enable in every new chat** marks the prompt as a default. It is off unless you turn it on.
2. In a chat, open the **Prompts** control in the composer tool row, right of the permissions dropdown. Tick what you want. The button shows the count.
3. The ticks apply from the next model step. No restart and no new session needed. Tick again, or press **Clear**, to take them out.
@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Usage：Prompts are matched by an id generated behind the scenes, not by title, so renaming a prompt keeps every session pointed at it.

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Defaults for new chats：A prompt can be set to start enabled. Every session that has never been ticked by hand opens with those defaults already on, and the picker shows them ticked, so the count on a fresh chat matches what that chat will use.

The first hand edit to a session, whether that is ticking, unticking or **Clear**, becomes that session's own choice and takes over from then on. Unticking the last default prompt records "none here" instead of falling back to the defaults you just removed.

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Subagents：A session that has ticks of its own uses exactly those, and an empty list counts as a choice. A session with no choice at all takes the choice of the nearest ancestor session, so a subagent inherits from the chat that started it. Only a whole line with no choice anywhere falls back to the defaults for new chats.

@stmol/dsh-prompt-lib README · Good to know：- **The settings file must be writable.** The Prompts page says so up front and disables its controls. In the composer, a write the host refuses shows the reason under the list, so an edit is never dropped silently.
- **The composer control hides itself** until the settings remote is mounted and has answered its first read, rather than show a count that is about to change.
- **There are size limits.** The editor caps one instruction at 8000 characters. The host applies that same cap, uses at most 100 prompts and reads at most 500 library entries when it renders. Anything past those limits contributes nothing to the model. Settings still shows, edits and keeps every entry.
- **Selections accumulate.** The plugin keeps one entry per session that has ever been ticked in, and never prunes them. An entry whose prompts were all deleted still means "inject nothing", so removing it would quietly bring back the defaults for that session.
